Splitting counter terms

A Symbolica-only reconstruction of the real collinear counter terms in splitting_counter_term_computation.tex. The hard Born contribution is opaque. The calculation manipulates only its external spin or polarization connector and replaces a recognized contraction by the scalar functions ||(\sigma(q)||) or ||(\sigma(g)||).

The notebook does not use SymPy, regular\nexpressions, or string-based algebra.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e"' data-kind='"info"'></marimo-callout-output>

1. Kinematics and conventions

The momentum fraction ||(x||) labels the daughter entering the hard interaction. The cut daughter carries ||(1-x||). With ||(s=2p_+\!\cdot p_-||), the coordinates are ||[ p=p_++\frac{p^2}{s}p_-,\qquad k=(1-x)p_++k_\perp+ \frac{|k_\perp|^2}{(1-x)s}p_-, ||]||[ p-k=xp_+-k_\perp+ \left(\frac{p^2}{s} -\frac{|k_\perp|^2}{(1-x)s}\right)p_-. ||]Equivalently, the momentum fraction used as the argument of every splitting kernel is defined by ||[ x=\frac{(p-k)\cdot p_-}{p\cdot p_-},\qquad 1-x=\frac{k\cdot p_-}{p\cdot p_-}. ||]Thus the hard momentum is ||(xp_+||) at leading collinear power, and the final kernels are already in the canonical form ||(P_{ij}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon)||); no final ||(x\leftrightarrow1-x||) relabelling is made. The virtualities ||(p^2||) and ||(|k_\perp|^2||) have the same collinear weight.

Color algebra

The contractions below are constructed with Spenso color representations and reduced by Idenso. The conventional labels are applied only after the reductions return the fundamental Casimir, generator index, or adjoint Casimir. Relative to the color-averaged Born identities, the relevant averages are ||[ \frac{1}{N_c}\sum_{i,j,a}T^a_{ij}T^a_{ji}=C_F, \qquad \frac{1}{N_A}\sum_{a,i,j}T^a_{ij}T^a_{ji}=T_R. ||]Thus the parent color averages are already contained in the conventional ||(C_F||) and ||(T_R||) coefficients shown below.We use the unregularized, azimuthally averaged CDR Altarelli--Parisi kernels of Eqs. (32)--(35) of Catani, Seymour and Trocsanyi, with ||(h_g=d-2=2(1-\epsilon)||) and ||(h_q=2||). Our labels use standard DGLAP ordering: the second index is the parent. Consequently the off-diagonal indices are transposed relative to that paper. Every ||(P_{ab}^{\mathrm{CDR}}||) below includes its color factor.

2. Black-box Born factorization

Here ||(k||) is the on-shell cut daughter, carrying longitudinal fraction ||(1-x||), while the daughter entering the Born black box has momentum ||(p-k||) and tends to ||(xp_+||) in the collinear limit. The tensors below are coupling-stripped, and every ||(\mathcal I^{R,V}||) denotes the coefficient of ||(a_s=\alpha_s/(2\pi)||). With two Cutkosky deltas and the dispersive virtuality measure, define ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal C_\epsilon &\equiv \frac{g_s^2}{a_s} \left(\frac{e^{\gamma_E}\mu^2}{4\pi}\right)^\epsilon \frac{(2\pi)^2}{2\pi}\\ &=16\pi^3 \left(\frac{e^{\gamma_E}\mu^2}{4\pi}\right)^\epsilon, \qquad \frac{g_s^2}{a_s}=8\pi^2. \end{aligned} ||]Every real contribution then starts from the normalized cut form ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal I_{ij}^{R} &={} \frac{g_s^2}{a_s} \left(\frac{e^{\gamma_E}\mu^2}{4\pi}\right)^\epsilon \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\frac{\mathrm dp^2}{2\pi p^2} \int\frac{\mathrm d^dk}{(2\pi)^d}\, \big[\mathcal T_{ij}\circ H_j\big](p,k)\, [2\pi\delta^+(k^2)]\, [2\pi\delta^{+\prime}((p-k)^2)]\\ &={}\mathcal C_\epsilon \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\frac{\mathrm dp^2}{p^2} \int\frac{\mathrm d^dk}{(2\pi)^d}\, \big[\mathcal T_{ij}\circ H_j\big](p,k)\, \delta^+(k^2)\,\delta^{+\prime}((p-k)^2). \end{aligned} ||]The virtual contribution is the two-particle cut of the external self-energy: ||[ \mathcal I_{ii}^{V}= \frac{\mathcal C_\epsilon}{2} \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\frac{\mathrm dp_1^2}{(p_1^2)^2} \int\frac{\mathrm d^dk}{(2\pi)^d}\, \big[\mathcal T_{ii}^{V}\circ H_i\big](p_1,k)\, \delta^+(k^2)\, \delta^+\!\left((p_1-k)^2\right). ||]Here ||(1/2||) is the one-external-leg factor and ||(\mathcal T_{ii}^V||) is the cut self-energy numerator. Its quark and gluon components are given in Section 4; the corresponding symmetry and flavor weights are applied in Section 6. For a gluon Born, ||(\mathcal T\circ H=\mathcal T^{\rho\sigma}H^g_{\rho\sigma}||); for a quark Born it denotes the corresponding Dirac trace. Thus ||(\delta^+(k^2)||) puts the emitted cut daughter on shell, whereas the differentiated cut ||(\delta^{+\prime}((p-k)^2)||) represents the squared propagator of the line entering the hard interaction. The black-box Born functions include their incoming color and spin averages. With ||(N_A=N_c^2-1||), ||[ \sigma(q)=\frac{1}{2N_c} \operatorname{Tr}_{s,c}[H_q\,x\slashed p_+], ||]||[ \sigma(g)=\frac{1}{(d-2)N_A} \Pi^{\mu\nu}H^g_{\mu\nu}. ||]For the hard daughter momentum ||(p-k||) and a lightlike reference ||(n||), the tensor ||[ \Pi^{\mu\nu}(p-k;n)=-g^{\mu\nu} +\frac{(p-k)^\mu n^\nu+n^\mu(p-k)^\nu}{(p-k)\cdot n} -(p-k)^2\frac{n^\mu n^\nu}{((p-k)\cdot n)^2} ||]is transverse to ||(p-k||) and is used to extract the scalar gluon Born; it is not an internal propagator. The spin factors multiplying the tensor reductions are ||(2/(d-2)||) for ||(D_{gq}||), ||(1/2||) for ||(D_{qg}||), and ||(1||) for ||(D_{qq}||) and ||(D_{gg}||); they include the conversion of the external spin sums to the averaged Born functions. The color averages are already included when the Idenso color contractions are reduced relative to the corresponding Born identity. Their remaining coefficients are ||(T_R||), ||(C_F||), and ||(C_A||); no additional ||(N_c||) or ||(N_A||) factor is applied. No expression inside ||(H_q||) or ||(H_g||) is constructed or inspected. The next section specifies the leading-power replacement under which ||(\mathcal T_{ij}\circ H_j||) becomes a scalar numerator multiplying ||(\sigma(q)||) or ||(\sigma(g)||).

3. Joint collinear approximation

Apply the joint scaling ||[ p^2\mapsto\lambda^2p^2,\qquad |k_\perp|^2\mapsto\lambda^2|k_\perp|^2,\qquad H_j(p-k)\mapsto H_j(xp_+). ||]Keeping the coefficient of ||(\lambda^2||) gives ||[ \big[\mathcal T_{ij}\circ H_j\big]_{\mathrm{LP}} =N_{ij}^{\mathrm{LP}}(x,p^2,|k_\perp|^2)\,\sigma(j). ||]The Symbolica audit finds that all four reduced real numerators are homogeneous in ||(p^2||) and ||(|k_\perp|^2||) and contain only this ||(\lambda^2||) term. Thus every result displayed below is already the joint collinear approximation.

4. Numerators

Real contributions

The four structures contracted with the black-box hard part in the master integral are ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T_{gq}&=(\slashed p-\slashed k)\gamma^\mu\slashed k \gamma^\nu(\slashed p-\slashed k)d_{\mu\nu}(p;n),\\ \mathcal T_{qg}^{\rho\sigma} &=d^{\rho\mu}(p-k;n)d^{\sigma\nu}(p-k;n) \operatorname{Tr}\!\left[ \slashed p\gamma_\mu\slashed k\gamma_\nu\right],\\ \mathcal T_{qq}&=(\slashed k-\slashed p)\gamma^\mu\slashed p \gamma^\nu(\slashed k-\slashed p)d_{\mu\nu}(k;n),\\ \mathcal T_{gg}^{\rho\sigma} &=\frac{1}{d-2} d^{\rho r}(p-k;n)d^{\sigma s}(p-k;n) V_{\alpha r\mu}(p,-(p-k),-k) V_{\beta s\nu}(p,-(p-k),-k) \Pi^{\alpha\beta}(p;n) \Pi^{\mu\nu}(k;n). \end{aligned} ||]Here ||(d_{\mu\nu}||) is the ordinary axial-gauge propagator numerator. The quark structures enter as ||(\operatorname{Tr}(H_q\mathcal T_{ij})||), while the gluon structures enter as ||(\mathcal T_{ij}^{\rho\sigma}H^g_{\rho\sigma}||). Spenso applies the Born projection of Section 2 without constructing either hard function. The table gives ||(N_{ij}^{\mathrm{LP}}||), including the displayed color and spin/Born factors. After the longitudinal on-shell integration, define ||(\mathcal J_{ij}||) as the remaining scalar prefactor from the original ||(\mathrm dp^2/p^2||) measure, the rescaling of ||(\delta^{+\prime}((p-k)^2)||), and the Born flux normalization: ||[ \mathcal J_{gq}=\mathcal J_{qq} =\frac{1}{2x^2(1-x)p^2},\qquad \mathcal J_{qg}=\mathcal J_{gg} =\frac{1}{2x(1-x)p^2}. ||]Thus the original cut integral becomes, at leading power, ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{ij}^{R}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} &=\mathcal C_\epsilon \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\frac{\mathrm dp^2}{p^2} \int\frac{\mathrm d^dk}{(2\pi)^d}\, N_{ij}^{\mathrm{LP}}\,\sigma(j)\, \delta^+(k^2)\,\delta^{+\prime}\!\left((p-k)^2\right)\\ &=\mathcal C_\epsilon \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\mathrm dp^2 \int\frac{\mathrm dx\,\mathrm d^{d-2}k_\perp}{(2\pi)^d}\, \underbrace{\mathcal J_{ij}N_{ij}^{\mathrm{LP}}}_{ \mathcal W_{ij}} \delta'\!\left( p^2-\frac{|k_\perp|^2}{x(1-x)} \right)\sigma(j). \end{aligned} ||]Hence ||(\mathcal W_{ij}||) is the complete scalar coefficient of the remaining differentiated on-shell constraint; it is not an additional numerator.

Virtual contributions

For ||(\eta=p_1+p_2||), every cut-gluon line uses ||[ d_{\mu\nu}(\ell;\eta)=-g_{\mu\nu} +\frac{\ell_\mu\eta_\nu+\eta_\mu\ell_\nu}{\ell\cdot\eta} -\eta^2\frac{\ell_\mu\ell_\nu}{(\ell\cdot\eta)^2}. ||]The tables below are live outputs of the Spenso/Idenso contractions and the Symbolica leading-power expansion. Define the scalar virtual numerator by ||[ \big[\mathcal T_{ii}^{V}\circ H_i\big]_{\mathrm{LP}} =N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2)\,\sigma(i). ||]After Born projection, the virtual master integral of Section 2 is ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{ii}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}}= {}&\frac{\mathcal C_\epsilon}{2} \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\frac{\mathrm dp_1^2}{(p_1^2)^2} \int\frac{\mathrm d^dk}{(2\pi)^d}\, N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2)\,\sigma(i)\, \delta^+(k^2)\, \delta^+\!\left((p_1-k)^2\right)\\ ={}&\frac{\mathcal C_\epsilon}{2} \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\mathrm dp_1^2 \int\frac{\mathrm dx\,\mathrm d^{d-2}k_\perp}{(2\pi)^d}\, \frac{N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2)} {2x(1-x)(p_1^2)^2}\, \delta\!\left( p_1^2-\frac{|k_\perp|^2}{x(1-x)} \right)\sigma(i). \end{aligned} ||]In the second line, ||(\delta^+(k^2)||) has fixed the longitudinal component of ||(k||), and the remaining delta has been rescaled with ||[ \delta^+\!\left((p_1-k)^2\right) =\frac{1}{x}\delta\!\left( p_1^2-\frac{|k_\perp|^2}{x(1-x)} \right). ||]Here ||(N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}||) denotes the relevant component, or their weighted sum when several cuts contribute.

||(D_{qq}||)

The open quark self-energy tensor is ||[ \mathcal T_{qq}^{V}=\slashed p_1\gamma^\mu (\slashed p_1-\slashed k)\gamma^\nu\slashed p_1 d_{\mu\nu}(k;\eta). ||]Projecting its open Dirac chain onto ||(\slashed p_1||) with the complementary vector ||(p_2||) gives, at leading power in ||(p_1^2||), ||[ N_{qq}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2) =2p_1^2P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon). ||]The table displays this computed scalar numerator.

||(D_{gg}||)

Before Born projection, the cut gluon- and quark-loop tensors are ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T_{gg,\alpha\beta}^{V,(gg)}={}& V_{\alpha\rho\mu}(p_1,-(p_1-k),-k) V_{\beta\sigma\nu}(p_1,-(p_1-k),-k) d^{\rho\sigma}(p_1-k;\eta)d^{\mu\nu}(k;\eta),\\ \mathcal T_{gg,\alpha\beta}^{V,(q\bar q)}={}& \operatorname{Tr}\!\left[ \slashed k\gamma_\alpha(\slashed p_1-\slashed k)\gamma_\beta\right]. \end{aligned} ||]For ||(c\in\{gg,q\bar q\}||), define the exact Born-projected scalar numerator by ||[ N_{gg}^{V,(c)}(p_1,k;\eta) \equiv\frac{1}{d-2}\Pi^{\alpha\beta}(p_1;\eta) \mathcal T_{gg,\alpha\beta}^{V,(c)}. ||]The corresponding leading-power reductions are ||[ \begin{aligned} N_{gg}^{V,\mathrm{LP},(gg)}(x,p_1^2) &=2p_1^2P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon),\\ N_{gg}^{V,\mathrm{LP},(q\bar q)}(x,p_1^2) &=2p_1^2P_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon). \end{aligned} ||]The second equation is for one quark flavor. Axial-gauge ghosts decouple, and the four-gluon tadpole has no two-particle collinear cut. The identical-particle and flavor weights are applied in Section 6.

5. Integrated real contributions

The ||(\delta^+(k^2)||) integration fixes the longitudinal component of ||(k||). With ||[ (p-k)^2=x(p^2-p_0^2),\qquad p_0^2=\frac{|k_\perp|^2}{x(1-x)},\qquad \mathcal W_{ij}=\mathcal J_{ij}N_{ij}^{\mathrm{LP}}, ||]||(p_0^2||) is therefore the value of the parent virtuality ||(p^2||) selected by the on-shell condition ||((p-k)^2=0||). The master integral of Section 2 becomes ||[ \mathcal I_{ij}^{R}= \mathcal C_\epsilon \int_0^{\Lambda^2}\mathrm dp^2 \int\frac{\mathrm dx\,\mathrm d^{d-2}k_\perp}{(2\pi)^d} \mathcal W_{ij}(x,p^2,|k_\perp|^2) \delta'(p^2-p_0^2)\,\sigma(j). ||]The ||(p^2||) integration is the equality ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal I_{ij}^{R} =\mathcal C_\epsilon \int\frac{\mathrm dx\,\mathrm d^{d-2}k_\perp}{(2\pi)^d} \Big[&-\left.\partial_{p^2}\mathcal W_{ij}\right|_{p^2=p_0^2} \Theta(\Lambda^2-p_0^2)\\ &+\mathcal W_{ij}(x,\Lambda^2,|k_\perp|^2) \delta(\Lambda^2-p_0^2)\Big]\sigma(j). \end{aligned} ||]The first line is the bulk contribution and the second is the cutoff boundary. Set ||(K=|k_\perp|^2||) and ||(d=4-2\epsilon||). Applying the angular measure and the Section 2 identity ||[ \mathcal C_\epsilon \frac{\pi^{1-\epsilon}}{(2\pi)^{4-2\epsilon} \Gamma(1-\epsilon)} =\frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}(\mu^2)^\epsilon} {\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} ||]directly to the preceding equality gives ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal I_{ij}^{R}={}& \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}(\mu^2)^\epsilon} {\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\int_0^\infty\mathrm dK\,K^{-\epsilon} \Bigg[-\left.\partial_{p^2}\mathcal W_{ij} \right|_{p^2=K/[x(1-x)]} \Theta\!\left(\Lambda^2-\frac{K}{x(1-x)}\right)\\ &\hspace{4.8cm}+\mathcal W_{ij}(x,\Lambda^2,K) \delta\!\left(\Lambda^2-\frac{K}{x(1-x)}\right) \Bigg]\sigma(j). \end{aligned} ||]The theta function fixes the bulk range, while the radial delta fixes ||(K=\Lambda^2x(1-x)||) with Jacobian ||(x(1-x)||). Performing both operations gives the next equality, ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal I_{ij}^{R}={}& \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}(\mu^2)^\epsilon} {\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\,\Bigg[ -\int_0^{\Lambda^2x(1-x)}\mathrm dK\,K^{-\epsilon} \left.\partial_{p^2}\mathcal W_{ij} \right|_{p^2=K/[x(1-x)]}\\ &\hspace{2.2cm}+x(1-x) [\Lambda^2x(1-x)]^{-\epsilon} \mathcal W_{ij}\!\left( x,\Lambda^2,\Lambda^2x(1-x)\right) \Bigg]\sigma(j). \end{aligned} ||]The delta has now disappeared. Define the common radial factor by the equality ||[ \mathcal R_\epsilon(x)= \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \left( \frac{\Lambda^2x(1-x)}{e^{\gamma_E}\mu^2} \right)^{-\epsilon}. ||]For every channel, the Symbolica reduction extracts the remaining power of ||(K||) as ||[ -\left.\partial_{p^2}\mathcal W_{ij}(x,p^2,K) \right|_{p^2=K/[x(1-x)]} =\frac{\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{ij}(x,\epsilon)}{K}. ||]Since ||(\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{ij}||) is independent of ||(K||), the radial integral can now be performed. The preceding equality becomes ||[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal I_{ij}^{R}={}&\int_0^1\mathrm dx\, \mathcal R_\epsilon(x) \Bigg[-\frac{\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{ij}(x,\epsilon)} {\epsilon} +x(1-x)\mathcal W_{ij}\!\left( x,\Lambda^2,\Lambda^2x(1-x)\right) \Bigg]\sigma(j). \end{aligned} ||]

Bulk terms

The coefficients ||(\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{ij}||) and the integrated terms ||(-\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{ij}\mathcal R_\epsilon(x) \sigma(j)/\epsilon||) are given by:

Cutoff-boundary terms

The cutoff term is evaluated in Feynman gauge: in the second term of the preceding ||(\mathcal I_{ij}^{R}||) equality, every axial-gauge projector numerator is replaced by its metric part ||(-g_{\mu\nu}||) before imposing ||(K=\Lambda^2x(1-x)||). Denote the resulting weight by ||(\mathcal W_{ij}^{(-g)}||). The bulk term is unchanged and still uses the complete axial-gauge numerator. Define the dimensionless, color-dressed boundary coefficient directly from that weight: ||[ B_{ij}^{(-g)}(x,\epsilon) =x(1-x)\mathcal W_{ij}^{(-g)}\!\left( x,\Lambda^2,\Lambda^2x(1-x)\right). ||]The boundary part of the preceding integral is therefore ||[ \left.\mathcal I_{ij}^{R}\right|_{\partial,-g} =\int_0^1\mathrm dx\, \mathcal R_\epsilon(x)\, B_{ij}^{(-g)}(x,\epsilon)\,\sigma(j). ||]The superscript ||((-g)||) records one retained metric projector; one entry is shown for every such projector. The four metric surfaces simplify to ||[ B_{gq}^{(-g)}=T_R,\qquad B_{qg}^{(-g)}=B_{qq}^{(-g)} =\frac{C_F(d-2)}{2}=C_F(1-\epsilon), ||]||[ B_{gg}^{(-g,-g,-g)}= -\frac{3C_A(3-2\epsilon)}{4(1-\epsilon)}. ||]For ||(D_{gg}||), ``metric only'' retains the metric term in each of its three gluon projectors before imposing the surface. What follows are the boundary coefficients ||(B_{ij}^{(-g)}||) and the integrated boundaries ||(\left.\mathcal I_{ij}^{R}\right|_{\partial,-g}||).

data.text/markdown:
6. Integrated virtual contributions

Continue the ||(\mathcal I_{ii}^{V}||) equality of Section 4 and define the color-dressed cut kernel by ||[ \mathcal P_i^{V}(x,\epsilon) =\frac{N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2)}{2p_1^2}. ||]With ||(K=|k_\perp|^2||), the ||(p_1^2||) delta and the remaining radial integral give the successive equalities ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{ii}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&\frac{1}{2} \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}(\mu^2)^\epsilon} {\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\int_0^{\Lambda^2}\mathrm dp_1^2 \int_0^\infty\mathrm dK\,K^{-\epsilon} \frac{N_{ii}^{V,\mathrm{LP}}(x,p_1^2)} {2x(1-x)(p_1^2)^2}\\ &\hspace{2.0cm}\times \delta\!\left(p_1^2-\frac{K}{x(1-x)}\right)\sigma(i)\\ ={}&\frac{1}{2} \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}(\mu^2)^\epsilon} {\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\, \mathcal P_i^V(x,\epsilon) \int_0^{\Lambda^2x(1-x)}\mathrm dK\,K^{-1-\epsilon} \sigma(i)\\ ={}&-\frac{\sigma(i)}{2\epsilon} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\, \mathcal R_\epsilon(x)\, \mathcal P_i^V(x,\epsilon). \end{aligned} ||]

||(D_{qq}||)

The two labels of the quark-gluon cut give ||[ \mathcal P_q^V(x,\epsilon) =P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon) +P_{gq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon). ||]These are the two daughter labelings of the same quark-gluon cut, not two self-energy graphs. Since ||(\mathcal R_\epsilon(x)=\mathcal R_\epsilon(1-x)||) and ||(P_{gq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon) =P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(1-x,\epsilon)||), the common equality becomes ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{qq}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&-\frac{\sigma(q)}{2\epsilon} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\,\mathcal R_\epsilon(x) \left[P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon) +P_{gq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon)\right]\\ ={}&-\frac{\sigma(q)}{\epsilon} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\,\mathcal R_\epsilon(x) P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon). \end{aligned} ||]The Born factor has no ||(x||) dependence, so the ||(x||) integral is performed exactly. The equality continues as ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{qq}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&-\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}} {\epsilon\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}C_F \Big[2\mathrm B(1-\epsilon,-\epsilon) -\mathrm B(1-\epsilon,1-\epsilon)\\ &\hspace{4.2cm} -(1+\epsilon)\mathrm B(2-\epsilon,1-\epsilon)\Big]\sigma(q)\\ ={}&\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon}C_F \left[\frac{2}{\epsilon^2}+\frac{3}{2\epsilon} +\frac{7-\pi^2}{2}+\mathcal O(\epsilon)\right]\sigma(q)\\ \equiv{}&\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \mathcal V_q(\epsilon)\,\sigma(q). \end{aligned} ||]

||(D_{gg}||)

The gluon cut and the two quark-antiquark labelings for each flavor give ||[ \mathcal P_g^V(x,\epsilon) =P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon) +2n_fP_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon). ||]The factor ||(2n_f||) counts the quark and antiquark labelings for each of the ||(n_f||) flavors. The common factor ||(1/2||) in ||(\mathcal I_{gg}^{V}||) leaves the ||(n_fP_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}||) term below. The common equality therefore specializes to ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{gg}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&-\frac{\sigma(g)}{2\epsilon} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\,\mathcal R_\epsilon(x) \left[P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon) +2n_fP_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon)\right]\\ ={}&-\frac{\sigma(g)}{\epsilon} \int_0^1\mathrm dx\,\mathcal R_\epsilon(x) \left[\frac{P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon)}{2} +n_fP_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}(x,\epsilon)\right]. \end{aligned} ||]Again ||(\sigma(g)||) factorizes, and the ||(x||) integral is exact. The equality continues as ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{gg}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&-\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \frac{e^{\gamma_E\epsilon}} {\epsilon\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Bigg\{C_A\left[ 2\mathrm B(2-\epsilon,-\epsilon) +\mathrm B(2-\epsilon,2-\epsilon)\right]\\ &\hspace{2.0cm}+\frac{n_fT_R}{1-\epsilon}\left[ 2\mathrm B(3-\epsilon,1-\epsilon) -\epsilon\mathrm B(1-\epsilon,1-\epsilon)\right]\Bigg\}\sigma(g)\\ ={}&\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \left[\frac{2C_A}{\epsilon^2} +\frac{11C_A-4T_Rn_f}{6\epsilon} +\frac{C_A(67-9\pi^2)}{18} -\frac{10T_Rn_f}{9}+\mathcal O(\epsilon)\right]\sigma(g)\\ \equiv{}&\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \mathcal V_g(\epsilon)\,\sigma(g). \end{aligned} ||]Only now introduce an external convolution fraction ||(\xi||). Let ||(\sigma_i(\xi)||) denote the Born function evaluated with incoming fraction ||(\xi||), so that ||(\sigma_i(1)=\sigma(i)||). The diagonal virtual kernel is defined by ||[ \begin{aligned} \left.\mathcal I_{ii}^{V}\right|_{\mathrm{LP}} ={}&\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \mathcal V_i(\epsilon)\sigma_i(1)\\ ={}&\int_0^1\mathrm d\xi\, \left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \mathcal V_i(\epsilon) \delta(1-\xi)\sigma_i(\xi)\\ \equiv{}&\int_0^1\mathrm d\xi\, D_{ii}^{V}(\xi)\sigma_i(\xi), \end{aligned} ||]and hence ||[ D_{ii}^{V}(\xi) =\left(\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}\right)^{-\epsilon} \mathcal V_i(\epsilon)\delta(1-\xi). ||]

7. Assembled NLO counterterm

The real and virtual terms already contain the common normalization ||(\mathcal C_\epsilon||) of Section 2 and the normalized radial weight ||(\mathcal R_\epsilon||) of Section 5. No factor is restored at this stage. Use ||(\bar\xi'=1-\xi'||). The state set contains the gluon and every separate quark and antiquark flavor, ||[ \mathfrak S_1=\{g,q_1,\bar q_1,\ldots,q_{n_f},\bar q_{n_f}\}. ||]The color-stripped kernels in the compact counterterm use the same index order as ||(D_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak q'}||). Thus the results of Section 1 are inserted through ||[ \begin{aligned} c_{qq}P_{qq}^{(0)}&=P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}},& c_{qg}P_{qg}^{(0)}&=P_{gq}^{\mathrm{CDR}},\\ c_{gq}P_{gq}^{(0)}&=P_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}},& c_{gg}P_{gg}^{(0)}&=P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}, \end{aligned} ||]with ||[ c_{gq}=T_R,\qquad c_{qg}=c_{qq}=C_F,\qquad c_{gg}=C_A. ||]The metric-projector boundaries of Section 5 give ||[ b_{\partial}^{gq}=1,\qquad b_{\partial}^{qg}=b_{\partial}^{qq}=1-\epsilon,\qquad b_{\partial}^{gg}=-\frac{3(3-2\epsilon)}{4(1-\epsilon)}, ||]because ||(c_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a}b_{\partial}^{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a} =B_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a}^{(-g)}||) for the first three channels and ||(c_{gg}b_{\partial}^{gg}=B_{gg}^{(-g,-g,-g)}||). The sum over ||(\mathfrak S_1||) reproduces the two virtual results of Section 6: for a quark it gives ||(P_{qq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}+P_{gq}^{\mathrm{CDR}}||), while for a gluon it gives ||(P_{gg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}+2n_fP_{qg}^{\mathrm{CDR}}||). The splitting counterterm uses the convention ||[ D^{(1)}=-\mathcal I_{\mathrm{bulk}}^R +\mathcal I_{\partial}^R+\mathcal I^V. ||]Thus the ||(-P/\epsilon||) produced by the raw real radial integral enters ||(D^{(1)}||) as ||(+P/\epsilon||), whereas the virtual self-energy retains the minus sign derived in Section 6. Combining the three terms gives ||[ \begin{aligned} D_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak q'}^{(1)}(\xi) &={} \left. \sum_{\mathfrak a\in\mathfrak S_1}\int_0^1\mathrm d\xi'\, \frac{c_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a}}{\Gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Bigg\{ \delta_{\mathfrak a\mathfrak q'}\delta(\xi-\xi') b_{\partial}^{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a} + \left[ \delta_{\mathfrak a\mathfrak q'}\delta(\xi-\xi') -\frac{\delta_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak q'}\delta(1-\xi)}{2} \right] \frac{P_{\mathfrak q\mathfrak a}^{(0)}(\xi')}{\epsilon} \Bigg\} \left( \frac{\Lambda^2\xi'\bar\xi'}{e^{\gamma_E}\mu^2} \right)^{-\epsilon} \right|_{\epsilon^0}. \end{aligned} ||]The finite-part operation is applied only after the regulated expression has been assembled.
